title: PRD addition: Quantifiable fallback budgets and synthetic verification for kernel regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: During a recent production degradation caused by an emergent kernel scheduling regression, multiple tenants experienced elevated tail latency and degraded throughput while autoscale attempted to recover. Postmortem action items called for concrete, testable PRD changes so future regressions surface earlier and trigger automated safe rollbacks.

Goal: Add measurable fallback budgets and a synthetic verification harness to the serving PRD to (1) detect kernel regressions before broad rollout, (2) limit blast radius with tenant-level fallback budgets, and (3) ensure automatic rollback and alerting when regressions exceed defined thresholds. This ticket converts postmortem recommendations into acceptance criteria, rollout gates, and runbook tests suitable for ship criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Define per-tenant 'fallback budget' concept and storage: API + DB fields to allocate a percentage of requests or token-budget for degraded-mode fallbacks (e.g., model-variant downgrade or cached-response) per tenant.

Specify canary verification suite: nightly synthetic traffic that validates kernel-level P50/P95/P99 latency and 99.9th token-generation latency for representative prompt sets; failures produce a failing canary.
Automated rollback gate: a release must be blocked if canary fails for 3 consecutive runs or if canary P99 exceeds baseline by > 2x for 10 minutes during rollout.

Runtime trigger thresholds: global auto-fallback if error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 min or tenant-level tail latency degrades > 150% of baseline for 5 min; actions documented in runbook with explicit steps for automatic or operator-triggered rollback.

Observability: dashboard that surfaces per-tenant fallback-budget consumption, canary pass/fail history, and time-series comparisons against pre-release baselines; alerts wired to oncall with runbook links.
Operator acceptance test: simulate kernel regression in staging, verify fallback budget enforcement, automated rollback, and synthetic verification detect-and-fail behavior end-to-end.
decisions: Adopt per-tenant fallback budgets rather than per-route to minimize config surface; budgets expressed as percentage of traffic and token allowance.
Canary will run in a dedicated cluster isolated from prod traffic but using the same kernel binaries and representative prompt cache to catch kernel regressions early.
Rollback policy: first attempt automated rollback to previous kernel on canary failure; if rollback fails, escalate to oncall and hold release until mitigations verified.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize data model for fallback budgets and canary specs; doc PRD updates and runbook changes.
Phase 1 (implementation): ENG implements budget enforcement, canary harness, and dashboard panels; create gates in release pipeline.
Phase 2 (staging verification): run chaos experiments and simulated kernel regressions in staging to validate acceptance tests.
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): enable on small percentage of releases with strict monitoring and manual oversight for 2 release cycles, then relax to automated gating.
Phase 4 (GA): make canary gating and fallback budgets part of runtime-1.20 shipping criteria.
